The first and most obvious characteristic of this card is that it comes at the end of all, and is therefore the complement of the Fool. It is attributed to the letter Tau. The two cards together accordingly spell the word Ath, which means Essence.
The letter Tau is attributed to Saturn, the outermost and slowest of the seven sacred planets; because of these dull, heavy qualities, the element of earth was thrust upon the symbol.

sections.title: Fire and Aries
sections.line: Crowley's attribution of Wands to Fire and to Aries.

quotes.text: The four suits are named as follows: “Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air; and “Disks” (“Coins”, or “Pantacles”), to Earth.
Thus, the Knight of Wands has the attribution of Aries, and represents swift violence of onset, the lightning flash.

sections.title: The flames of the Ace
sections.line: Crowley's description of the Ace of Wands: the flames as Yods and the solarphallic outburst of flame.

quotes.text: These flames are Yods, arranged in the form of the Tree of Life.
It is a solarphallic outburst of flame from which spring lightnings in every direction.
These elements are represented in the Hebrew alphabet by the letters Shin, Mem and Aleph.
The letter Shin, which is the letter of Fire, has to do double duty by representing Spirit as well.

family:tiphareth.line: Beauty, the Son and the Sun: the sixth sephira at the centre of the Tree, the only one below the Abyss in direct touch with the Crown, and consciousness in its most balanced form. Its number gives each suit its element in harmonious success: Victory in Wands, Pleasure in Cups, Science in Swords, Success in Disks. Among the ten bodies of the solar system on the Tree, it is the Sun.

quotes.text: This Sephira is in some respects the most important of all. It is the centre of the whole system; it is the only Sephira below the Abyss which communicates directly with Kether. It is fed directly from Chokmah and Binah; also from Chesed and Geburah.

In the planetary system it represents the Sun; in the system of Tetragrammaton it represents the Son. The entire geometrical complex of the Ruach may be regarded as an expansion from Tiphareth. It represents consciousness in its most harmonized and balanced form; definitely in form, not only in idea, as in the case of the number Two. In other words, the Son is an interpretation of the Father in terms of the mind.
The Ruach is centred in the airy Sephira, Tiphareth, who is the Son, the first‐born of the Father, and the Sun, the first emanation of the creative Phallus.
The Sefira Tifereth is the King, and in the usual arrangement of the Sefiroth he occupies the second place: Kether Tifereth Yesod Malchuth.
The figure of Tifereth belongs to the Sefiroth system, which is conceived to be a tree. Tifereth occupies the middle position.
Yesod is as a part to the whole, and the whole is Tifereth, who is named the sun.
This picture represents the Tree of Life, which is a map of the Universe.
Hitherto, the main theme of this essay has been the Tree of Life, in its essence the Sephiroth.
The Tree of Life can be divided into four planes: the number I corresponds to Fire; numbers 2 and 3, to Water; numbers 4 to 9, to Air; and the number 10 to Earth.
The number I is Atziluth, the Archetypal World; but the number 2, as being the dynamic aspect of the number I, is the Practical attribution.

sections.title: In Jung
sections.line: CW14 ¶18 (the list Kether, Tifereth, Yesod, Malchuth), ¶158 (the arbor philosophica and the tree of the Sefiroth), ¶592 and ¶652 (Adam Kadmon and the system of the Sefiroth in three columns).

quotes.text: Kether, the Crown, corresponds to the upward-growing root of the Tree of the Sefiroth.
The Sefira Tifereth is the King, and in the usual arrangement of the Sefiroth he occupies the second place: Kether Tifereth Yesod Malchuth.
Adam Kadmon is either the whole tree or is thought of as the mediator between the supreme authority, En Soph, and the Sefiroth.

On the other hand it is evident that the Lunatica is closely connected with the “tree of the sea” in Arabian alchemy207 and hence with the arbor philosophica, which in turn has parallels with the Cabalistic tree of the Sefiroth209 and with the tree of Christian mysticism210 and Hindu philosophy.

Hence Adam Kadmon, as a personification of the whole “inverted tree,” is androgynous, but the system itself is a highly differentiated coniunctio symbol, and, as such, divided into three parts (three columns of three Sefiroth each).

sections.title: The ten as the numbers
sections.line: Jung, CW10 ¶692: the numbers one to ten in the traditional symbolism. Von Franz, Number and Time: ten as the whole multiplicity of existence, and the sephiroth as the ten primal numbers, spheres of the unknowable primal one.

quotes.text: Ten is the perfect unfolding of unity, and the numbers one to ten have the significance of a completed cycle.
For this purpose Fa-tzang makes use of the symbol of ten copper coins (ch’ien), in which ten here signifies the whole inexhaustible multiplicity of existence.

Totality It is common knowledge that in the cabala the ten primal numbers, the sephiroth, are considered to be emanations of divine immaterial origin in the sense that the “original one” remains far removed from all things and only manifests its various aspects in each single sepbira.
They are “spheres” and “totalities” of the unknowable primal one.
The Abyss—between Ideal and Actual.
For below the Abyss, contradiction is division; but above the Abyss, contradiction is Unity.
Saturn is in the position of the non‐existent Sephira, Daäth,
His position on the Tree of Life shows the third Sephira, Binah, Understanding, as not yet formulated; still less the false Sephira, Da’ath, knowledge.

family:virgo.line: Virgo is Mutable Earth, the quiet turn of the year toward harvest and reflection. It searches for meaningful service: work done with patience, skill and humility that heals and makes whole. Its gift is the craft of Hermes, turning humble clay into a work of perfection; its shadow is the critic and the worrier, a mind that neglects the body and the heart. Mercury is its mundane ruler and the nurturing Moon its esoteric one.

quotes.text: In the process of alchemical purification Hermes’ virtues are those of the Virgo archetype: patience, purification or perfectionism, meticulous attention to technique and procedure, obedience to methodology, industriousness, and most important, humility.

Leo was active, dynamic and most of all, in control. Virgo is Mutable, or passive-responsive to events and circumstances, especially those involved with the Sixth House of labor, health, service and study.

Hermes can take the common soil of Virgo Earth, humble clay, and fashion from it a work of perfection. My experience of those who participate in the Virgo archetype through either planets in Virgo or Sixth House planets has been that they can do the smallest, most ordinary or commonplace job with such detailed, skilled precision that they make of it an art. Behind many a shy, simple Virgo personality hides magical Hermes.

When Virgo feels that his/her work is not useful, or meaningful to him/her, that s/he is no longer learning or growing in some way, his/her body begins to exhibit symptoms as a warning that a change is needed. The body is a barometer of the satisfaction or lack of it in the various meanings of the Sixth House.

In this myth, Isis does nothing by her own authority. She is a humble vehicle, the Temple of Horus through which healing techniques come. The Virgo Goddess studies, waits, prays, has faith (Pisces polarity), and responds efficiently and appropriately in a crisis.

People are imperfect, and when Virgo is too critical, they may become too depressed to improve. As Virgo progresses in integrating Piscean inner peace and faith, many self-doubts disappear. The ego begins to depend upon God more and to rely less on its own resources.

Those Virgos who are true lunar intuitives, true nurturers combine the Hermes’ discrimination and magical power to transform, to heal, with the caring nature of the Moon. They encourage others to believe in themselves and develop their resources.
Virgo When man is roaring like a lion there is nothing better to tame him than a virgin.

cite.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

quotes.text: When the sun came into Pisces, Virgo became the autumnal sign, and astrology has connected that fact with the worship of the Virgin Mary.

cite.workTitle: Dream Analysis: Notes of the Seminar

family:water.line: Water in Jung's sources: the aqua permanens, the living and dissolving water, the unconscious, and water and spirit.

quotes.text: This account makes one thing very evident: the philosophical water is the stone or the prima materia itself; but at the same time, it is also its solvent
Therefore in alchemy Mercurius is sometimes a “spirit” and sometimes a “water,” the so-called aqua permanens, which is none other than argentum vivum.
The water of life has its parallel in the aqua permanens of alchemy.

cite.workTitle: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious

quotes.text: There can be no doubt that this is the aqua permanens or aqua pontica, the primal water which contains the four elements.

sections.title: Living and dissolving
sections.line: The water as a living being that kills and vivifies, and that dissolves the body into spirit: CW12 ¶94; CW14 ¶359 and ¶318.

quotes.text: They called it aqua nostra, mercurius vivus, argentum vivum, vinum ardens, aqua vitae, succus lunariae, and so on, by which they meant a living being not devoid of substance, as opposed to the rigid immateriality of mind in the abstract.
But of the aqua permanens it was said: “It kills and vivifies.”
The “Gloria mundi” says: “The mystery of every thing is life, which is water; for water dissolves the body into spirit and summons a spirit from the dead.”

sections.title: Water and the unconscious
sections.line: The sea or a large expanse of water as the unconscious, and the mother and the water of life: CW14 ¶342; CW5 ¶320; CW12 ¶92.

quotes.text: The psychological equivalent of the chaotic water of the beginning684 is the unconscious, which the old writers could grasp only in projected form, just as today most people cannot see the beam in their own eye but are all too well aware of the mote in their brother’s. Political propaganda exploits this primitivity and conquers the naive with their own defect.
In dreams and fantasies the sea or a large expanse of water signifies the unconscious.
Just as the father represents collective consciousness, the traditional spirit, so the mother stands for the collective unconscious, the source of the water of life23 (fig. 25).
Water and spirit are often identical.
The water is a soul or spirit, that is, a psychic “substance,” which now in its turn is applied to the initial material.
The meaning of the ten numbers is as follows: “1: the spirit of the Living God; 2: spirit from spirit; 3: water from spirit; 4: fire from water; 5–10: height, depth, East, West, South, North.”
quotes.voice: Numbers as quoted from a source by Jung

quotes.text: In the language of the alchemists, however, spirit and water are synonymous, as they are in the language of the early Christians, for whom water meant the spiritus veritatis.

family:yesod.line: The Foundation: the ninth sephira, back on the middle pillar beneath Tiphareth, where the energies above crystallise in the formative world of images. Its number gives each suit the full impact of its force, balanced once more: Strength in Wands, Happiness in Cups, Cruelty in Swords, Gain in Disks. Among the ten bodies of the solar system on the Tree, it is the Moon.

quotes.text: These cards are attributed to Yesod. After the double excursion into misfortune, the current returns to the middle pillar. This Sephira is the seat of the great crystallization of Energy. But it takes place very far down the Tree, at the apex of the third descending triangle, and a flat triangle at that. There is little help from low, unbalanced spheres like Netzach and Hod.

What saves Yesod is the direct ray from Tiphareth; this Sephira is in the direct line of succession. Each of these cards gives the full impact of the elemental force, but in its most material sense; that is, of the idea of the force, for Yesod is still in Yetzirah, the formative world.
This card is referred to Yesod, the Foundation; this brings the Energy back into balance. The Nine represents always the fullest development of the Force in its relation with the Forces above it.

The Number Nine, Yesod, in the suit of Water, restores the stability lost by the excursions of Netzach and Hod from the Middle Pillar. It is also the number of the Moon, thus strengthening the idea of Water.

“Jezoth” (= Yesod) is the ninth and middle Sefira in the lowest triad of the Cabalistic tree, and was interpreted as the creative and procreative power in the universe. Alchemically he corresponds to the spiritus vegetativus, Mercurius.
Yesod unites the emanation of the right, masculine side (Nezach, life-force) with the left, feminine side (Hod, beauty).

water-quaternity.text: Whereas the original tetrameria corresponded exactly to the quaternity of elements, it was now frequently stressed that although there were four elements (earth, water, fire, and air) and four qualities (hot, cold, dry, and moist), there were only three colours: black, white, and red.
